SELECT
    MIN(c.region) AS region,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS buyers
FROM {{ source('legacy', 'customers') }} c
JOIN {{ source('legacy', 'orders') }} o
    ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY UPPER(RTRIM(c.region))

history.sql:
SELECT
    MIN(c.region) AS region,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_id) AS buyers
FROM {{ source('legacy', 'customers') }} c
JOIN {{ source('legacy', 'orders') }} o
    ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY UPPER(RTRIM(c.region))

explanation: This procedure counts how many distinct customers have placed at least one order in each sales region, and saves the result as a table. Because SQL Server compares text without regard to letter case or trailing spaces, regions that differ only in those ways are treated as one region, so the model groups them the same way. The region label shown for each group is one representative spelling from that group.
